products.name: Pic Hider
products.tagline: Private photo & video vault — locked behind your PIN
products.description: Hide photos and videos behind a PIN-encrypted vault (AES-256). Fingerprint/face unlock (works on Class-2 sensors too), built-in viewer with zoom and video playback, and one-tap export back to your gallery. v1.3.1 is the durability pass: vault creation is a single atomic verified write with full rollback, broken half-written vaults self-heal, imports stream to disk (huge videos no longer OOM), unlocks run off the main thread, and the viewer decodes photos at screen size. Plus app disguise (Calculator / Notes / Gallery / custom icon) and recovery question.

notes: The REAL 'PIN won't save' fix: vault creation is now ONE atomic, verified write (index first, setup flag last, disk result checked, full rollback) — a kill or full disk can no longer fake a successful setup
Self-heal: a vault corrupted by the old partial writes is detected at launch, reset cleanly and the wizard tells you what happened (no more permanently-unlockable lock screen)

The REAL 'gallery won't open' hardening: the import guard survives process death mid-pick, thumbnails and durations read straight from the picker's file descriptor, and a half-typed PIN survives dark-mode/split-screen flips

Big imports stream-encrypt to disk (a 500 MB video used to run out of memory mid-import), the viewer decodes photos off the main thread at screen size, and every unlock/key change runs off the frozen-free path
FIXED 'gallery won't open': phones whose gallery picker silently fails now get a one-tap file-browser fallback
FIXED 'PIN won't save': synchronous vault writes — an aggressive memory killer can never eat a fresh setup
Setup failures show a clear in-wizard message; the lock screen always keeps a manual Unlock button
Photo import + custom shortcut icons fixed on every phone
Step-by-step professional PIN setup wizard
Fingerprint login works on Class-2 (budget) sensors
App disguise — Calculator / Notes / Gallery launcher looks
AES-256-GCM PIN vault, biometric unlock, encrypted viewer, export

products.name: Ophelia Widgets
products.tagline: 31 hand-crafted widgets — now with the NewThing-style DOT MATRIX set
products.description: 38 home-screen widgets in the Ophelia red-on-black look — clocks, weather, battery, notes, tools, gauges, fun — plus TWO full Nothing-style DOT MATRIX batches. v1.5.1: photo frames survive reboots, battery/weather scheduling is single-source and reboot-proof, the sun widget's timezone flip survives reschedules, and the dot widgets' rendering is thread-safe. Everything is offline-first: no accounts, no analytics.

notes: Photo frame widgets survive reboots — picked photos are copied into the app's private storage at pick time (Android 13+ photo-picker grants were never persistable, the old widget went blank after a restart)
Battery widgets re-arm correctly after reboot (Ophelia-battery-only setups were frozen) and weather/battery stop quadruple-fetching (one scheduling source)
Sun widget's city-timezone midnight flip survives other widgets' reschedules; step counter's sensor listener no longer leaks and resets its baseline after reboot
Currency arrows work for rates ≥ 1000 and empty picks no longer silently no-op in the shortcut/dial configs
Sunrise/Sunset now runs in the CITY’s own timezone — pick Tokyo on an Indian phone and the times are Tokyo wall-clock, not IST
Live NOW line on the sun tile (city’s current time, refreshes hourly) + short UTC offset next to the city name (TOKYO +9)
Zone-aware midnight scheduling: the day flips at the CITY’s local midnight, not just the phone’s
Config screen shows the resolved IANA zone after lookup; older widgets keep working (fall back to the phone zone)
NEW Game Score widget — two-team scoreboard with +/− keys and centre reset
NEW Hydro tracker — tap to log glasses, opt-in reminder notifications
NEW Currency Rate (USD→INR live, 6-hour refresh, change arrows) and Sunrise/Sunset (offline solar math)
NEW Days Since, Week Number and Uptime — 7 new widgets, 38 total
NEW DOT MATRIX batch (8 widgets, 31 total): App Shortcut, App Folder, Month Calendar, Step Counter, Now Playing, Web Search, AI Bar, Contact Dial
Now Playing: transport keys steer whatever app is playing; track titles via optional notification access
AI Bar: Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot and Claude in one tile
Launcher icon = the real Ophelia artwork
+11 widgets: Ophelia brand set, year/day/moon progress, world clock, storage & RAM gauges, tally, decision spinner

products.name: Junk Cleaner
products.tagline: Smart clean · duplicates · SIMILAR PHOTOS + VIDEOS (no root)
products.description: Storage rescue without root: junk scan (thumbnail caches, empty folders, leftover installers, temp files), the 25 biggest files, byte-identical duplicate finder, SIMILAR PHOTOS (perceptual hash) and SIMILAR VIDEOS (keyframe fingerprints) — v1.4.1 deletes through MediaStore so the gallery stays clean, handles Android 10 properly, and hardens the folder-safety filter. Each group keeps the LARGEST copy; deletion goes through the app's confirmation AND Android's own delete sheet. Nothing is ever removed silently.

notes: MediaStore-aware deletes for Big Files & Duplicates — photos and videos leave the gallery database properly (no more broken 'ghost' thumbnails after cleaning)
Android 10 fixed: legacy-storage flag + the system's own permission sheet when another app's media needs a grant
Safety: empty-folder cleaning can never delete new files that arrived after the scan, and hidden .vault-style folders are actually skipped now
Storage overview refreshes after every clean (not just CLEAN ALL) and the app's own clean keeps its JIT profiles
SIMILAR VIDEOS — the heavy hitters: re-sent and re-encoded copies of the SAME clip now group up (one 200 MB re-send chain frees more than every photo group combined)
4 keyframes sampled across each video's timeline, fingerprinted with the photo pipeline; flat frames are dropped so two 'opens on black' clips can't false-group
Duration gate (±1.5 s or ±8%) + both-directions 3-of-4 frame agreement — trimmed re-cuts are deliberately NOT grouped
keeper = the largest file · live progress while fingerprinting · Android's own delete sheet on 30+ · 20 new tests (55 total green)
SIMILAR PHOTOS: perceptual-hash review — burst shots, HDR takes and WhatsApp re-sends grouped even when bytes differ
Each group keeps the LARGEST copy (least compressed); a '% alike' chip shows how close they are
Deletion is double-confirmed: the app's dialog, then Android's own system delete sheet (API 30+)
Live progress while fingerprinting the library ('Fingerprinting 320/1,245 photos…') + unreadable-image skip count
The app now asks for real Android permissions (Photos & videos, Music & audio) with a one-tap card — the app-info Permissions page lists them properly instead of showing 'no permissions requested'.
New launcher icon: your own Junk Cleaner artwork, full-bleed adaptive icon.
All v1.1.0 features unchanged: Big Files top-25, hash-verified duplicate finder, cache boost, per-app cache dashboard.
NEW BIG FILES: the 25 largest files on storage, per-file confirm delete
NEW DUPLICATES: byte-identical copies (size + full-hash verified), keep-first one-tap clean with review

products.name: EasyPair
products.tagline: Offline high-speed sharing — no data, no limits, and interrupted transfers RESUME
products.description: Offline file sharing with zero limits — Wi-Fi Direct, hotspot, same Wi-Fi, USB cable or Bluetooth, no router and no data needed. Photos, videos, audio, files, folders, installed apps (APK) and clipboard text. v1.6.1 fixes the resume identity check (fragmented first reads hashed the wrong bytes, so interrupted big transfers restarted from zero), guards truncated small-file saves, and cleans up the group-owner send path. v1.6.0's resume engine, v1.5.0's encrypted TLS receiver and full LocalSend v2 interop are all intact.

notes: RESUME actually resumes: the partial-file head hash was computed with the wrong buffer offsets, so it never matched the sender's proof on fragmented (Bluetooth / slow Wi-Fi) reads — resume silently fell back to restart-from-zero. The hash math is fixed and unit-tested
A dropped small file is now reported as failed (connection dropped at X of Y) instead of being saved as a truncated 'success'
Wi-Fi Direct group-owner sends no longer push 0-byte extras; the About card shows the real version
NEW: PARTIAL-FILE RESUME — interrupted transfers continue from the exact byte, never from zero
Big files (8 MB+) are received into a private .part buffer; a drop at 80% of a video keeps those bytes safe
RESUME TRANSFER card on Home + Queue after a failed batch — one tap and only the missing tail travels
Same-file proof: first-4KB SHA-256 must match, so a different file with the same name can never corrupt a partial; stale partials (14 days) self-clean
NEW: ENCRYPTED RECEIVER — flip 'Encrypted receiver (HTTPS)' in Settings and EasyPair itself serves LocalSend behind TLS
Certificate is generated in the Android Keystore (hardware-backed where available); the private key never leaves your phone
Our announcement now carries the certificate's real SHA-256 — LocalSend and EasyPair senders PIN us, nothing travels in the clear
Default OFF (LocalSend's own default): plain-HTTP interop keeps working exactly as before until you opt in
NEW: ENCRYPTED LOCALSEND — LocalSend receivers that enable HTTPS mode are now supported
REAL certificate pinning: the announced SHA-256 fingerprint must match the presented certificate or the handshake is refused — never trust-all
Encrypted peers show a lock + 'encrypted' badge in the nearby device list
8 new tests including a real self-signed HTTPS server round-trip (pinned pass / wrong-pin reject / unpinned reject)
NEW: LocalSend interop — receive from the LocalSend app on Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android (multicast discovery 224.0.0.167, HTTP REST v2.2 on port 53317)
NEW: send TO any LocalSend receiver over HTTP REST (prepare-upload + upload, both wire generations supported)
NEW: incoming LocalSend files verified with SHA-256 when the sender provides a hash, saved to Downloads/LocalSend and listed in Received Files
27 new JVM protocol tests; gesture/UI untouched — same look, same flow
